title: Mechanistic interpretability: induction heads
summary: Reverse-engineer the actual circuit in a small transformer that implements in-context learning. By the end you'll have an activation-patching pipeline, a circuit identification, and a write-up with falsifiable ablation results.
contentIntro:
## What you'll build

A mech-interp project at researcher quality: identify the induction circuit in a small open transformer, validate it with activation patching, and write up the result with the rigor of a published paper.

Four milestones, ~5 weeks. By the end you'll have:

- A working TransformerLens-based analysis pipeline
- Identification of the previous-token + induction head pair in a 2-layer transformer
- Causal-mediation evidence (activation patching) showing the heads are responsible
- A write-up with falsifiable ablation claims

## What you'll build

Four milestones, each producing a notebook + writeup. By the end your artifact page is a research-quality reverse-engineering of a small transformer's induction circuit.

## Format

Use TransformerLens (the standard mech-interp library) and an open small model (Pythia-160M, GPT-2 small, or a model you train yourself in milestone 1). Single GPU is plenty.

## Why this capstone

Mech-interp is one of the most credible research areas in AI safety + alignment. It's also a slow-publication area where one well-validated finding makes a real contribution. This capstone walks you through the canonical example (induction heads) with full methodological depth — so you can read frontier interp papers + design your own follow-ups.

contentGrad:
## What you'll build

A reproduction of Olsson et al. 2022's induction-heads result on a 2-layer model of your own choosing, with full methodological discipline. Defense covers: why you trust the evidence, what alternative interpretations exist, what the result generalizes to.

milestones.title: Pick (or train) a 2-layer transformer + set up TransformerLens
milestones.description:
Either: (a) load a small open model — Pythia-160M, GPT-2 small — that already shows induction-like behavior, or (b) train your own 2-layer transformer on a copy task or simple text dataset.

Verify the model exhibits the induction pattern: prompt with `"A B ... A"` and confirm the model assigns higher probability to `B` next than to alternatives. This is your *behavior* — the thing you'll explain mechanically.

Build a TransformerLens-compatible loader for your model. Run a small evaluation set (50-100 prompts) to establish baseline behavior.

Writeup: explain why you picked this model, show the behavioral evaluation, and demonstrate your TransformerLens pipeline working on a single example.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the chosen model exhibits the induction behavior and the behavioral baseline is established.
Score whether the TransformerLens setup is working: can the learner extract attention patterns, intermediate activations, and run interventions?
Score the writeup's clarity in explaining the setup choice and providing reproducible code.

milestones.title: Identify previous-token heads in layer L
milestones.description:
Find the heads in your model's first layer (layer L) that implement 'attend to the previous token.'

Methodology:
- For each head, compute the attention pattern on a sample of inputs
- Score each head by how much weight it puts on position-1 (the previous token) on average
- Identify the head(s) with the strongest previous-token pattern

Visualize the attention patterns of your top candidates as heatmaps. The pattern should be a diagonal shifted by one — clearly distinct from generic local-attention heads.

Writeup: show the candidate heads, the heatmaps, and your scoring method. Be honest about ambiguity — if multiple heads have weak previous-token patterns rather than one having a strong one, say so.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the previous-token-head identification is methodologically sound. Is the scoring metric defensible? Are multiple heads compared rather than just confirming a hypothesis?
Score the quality of the attention pattern visualizations.
Score whether the writeup honestly characterizes the strength of the evidence.

milestones.title: Identify induction heads in layer L+1
milestones.description:
Find the heads in layer L+1 that compose with the previous-token heads to implement induction.

Methodology:
- For each head in layer L+1, score its attention pattern on inputs of the form `"A B ... A"`
- The head should attend from the second `A` *back to* the first `A` (the matching token)
- Critically, it should attend to position `i` such that token at position `i` matches the current token — this is content-based attention

Visualize the attention patterns. Confirm at least one head shows the matching-token pattern.

Writeup: show the identified head, characterize how strongly it implements induction, and discuss the composition with the previous-token head from milestone 2.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the induction head is correctly identified by content-based attention to matching tokens, not just generic patterns.
Score whether the writeup explains how the L+1 induction head composes with the L previous-token head to produce the observed behavior.
Score the clarity of the writeup and figures.

milestones.title: Activation patching + falsifiable ablation
milestones.description:
Run activation patching to causally validate the circuit:

- For each candidate head (previous-token + induction), patch its activations from a *different* input. If the head is causally responsible for induction, patching should disrupt the behavior.
- Score how much the model's induction probability degrades when each head is patched.
- The two heads identified in milestones 2 and 3 should be the highest-impact heads.

Then do explicit ablation: zero out (or noise out) the candidate heads and confirm the induction behavior breaks.

In your writeup, present a falsifiable claim: 'Heads X and Y are causally responsible for induction in this model. Ablating either removes the behavior.' Show the supporting evidence + acknowledge the alternative interpretations (could other heads do the same thing redundantly?).

This is the milestone where engineering meets research. The grader looks for methodological discipline, not just 'we found a circuit.'

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether activation patching is set up correctly: appropriate replacement source, proper measurement of the downstream effect, full sweep over candidate heads.
Score the ablation evidence: do the experiments support a causal claim? Are alternative interpretations addressed?
Score the rigor of the final claim. Is it falsifiable? Are limitations acknowledged? Is the methodology defensible?
